DI BACONC "UPWAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. ML- SEP 16 2025 RIZALYN PRADO ("YZZAY PRADO") yzzayprado@gmail.com Dear Ms. Prado. S. 2029 This refers to your e-mail referred by the Commission on Election (Comelec) to this Department. Per your e-mail, you narrated that the Barangay Captain of your Municipality ran for and was elected as Municipal Councilor which then created a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Punong Barangay. You also stated that the Sangguniang Barangay Member who obtained the highest number of votes during the last barangay election should assume the vacant position of Punong Barangay. Thereafter, the resultant vacancy in the Sangguniang Barangay should be filled successively based on the ranking of votes from ISt up to 6th position and until the 7th position became vacant. According to you, rather than appointing the 8th-ranked losing candidate to the now-vacant 7th Barangay Kagawad position, your Congressman purportedly designated an individual who did not even ran in the preceding barangay election. At the outset, Section 44 of Republic Act (RA) No. 71601 states that a permanent vacancy arises when an elective official fills a higher vacant office, among others. This Department now opines in seriatim. On Whether a Member of Congress Can Validly Appoint a Person to Fill a Vacancy in the Sangguniang Barangay We opine in the neqative. A Member of Congress does not possess the legal authority to appoint any official of the Sangguniang Barangay. Section 45(d) of RA 7160 explicitly states that a permanent vacancy in the Sangguniang Barangay shall be filled by appointment of the City or Municipal Mayor upon the recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concerned. The said provision is clear and unambiguous, thereby leaving no room for construction. Where the law speaks in clear and categorical language, there is no occasion for interpretation; there is only room for application.2 Under the rule of statutory construction of expressio unius est exclusion alterius, the Congressman is bereft of any legal authority to appoint any person as Barangay I Otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991." 2 Abello, et al. v. Commissioner, G.R. No. 120721, February 23, 2005. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Kagawad or a member of the Sangguniang Barangay precisely because such power is expressly conferred only to the City or Municipal Mayor, as the case may be. "It is a settled rule of statutory construction that the express mention of one person, thing, or consequence implies the exclusion of all others. The rule is expressed in the familiar maxim, expressio unjus est exclusio alterius. xxx x x x They proceed from the premise that the legislature would not have made specified enumeration in a statute had the intention been not to restrict its meaning and confine its terms to those expressly mentioned."3 (Emphasis ours) In light of the foregoing, only the City or Municipal Mayor shall appoint an individual to the 7th vacant Barangay Kagawad position upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay. On Whether the Losing Candidate Who Ranked 8th in the Last Barangay Election Should Be Appointed to the Resultant 7th- Kagawad Vacant Position The answer is likewise in the negative. Under Section 45 of RA 7160, in case a permanent vacancy occurs in the Sangguniang Barangay, the rule of succession must first be applied. This will result in the vacancy of the 7th position. The rule of succession is not anymore applicable because the Number 8 Sangguniang Barangay candidate in the last election was not proclaimed as winner by the COMELEC. Hence, he or she has no rank upon which the succession is based. Pursuant to Section 45(a)(3) of RA 7160, the 7th vacant position shall be filled up by appointment to be issued by the City or Municipal Mayor upon the recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concerned.4 Further, the phraseology of Section 45(a)(3) must be interpreted according to the clear and plain meaning of the language or words used. The provision does not state, directly or impliedly, that the 8th-ranked losing Sangguniang Barangay candidate should be considered for automatic appointment in case of permanent vacancy for the 7th Barangay Kagawad position. Verba legis non est recedendum, or from the words of a statute there should be no departure. Therefore, the 8th-ranked losing Sangguniang Barangay candidate is not entitled to automatic appointment to the 7th-Barangay Kagawad position. As the law provides, the vacancy must be filled through appointment by the City or Municipal Mayor, as the case may be, upon recommendation of the Sanggunian Barangay. This letter reply is rendered solely for academic discussion purposes without prejudice to any contrary interpretation of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to guide you accordingly. 3 Malinias v. The Commission on Elections, et al., G.R. No. 1469943, October 4, 2002. 4 Barangay Primer, 6th Ed., 2018, pp. 28. Page 2 of 3
